source_profile: US adult men, all ages, all regions. Composition read from the GENDER row across the Gen Pop file and the male cuts of the profile corpus (Reba McEntire - Male, Shark Tank - Male, Protein Enthusiasts - Male, Kardashians - Male), triangulated against the gender splits that platforms and measurement firms publish for their own audiences.
one_line: US adult men, 18 and up, every generation together. About 49 percent of US adults. This lens is not a taste filter: every item stays on the board, and each item is re-valued to the share of its audience that is men, then re-ranked by that number. The job is to get the SHARE right for each item, item by item, from what is known about who actually watches, listens, reads, plays, buys and searches for it.

demographics.age_range: 18 to 80 plus, weighted like the US adult population: roughly a fifth each in 18-29, 30-44, 45-59 and 60 plus, with men outnumbered by women above 65.
demographics.gender_skew: 100 percent men by definition. The baseline share of any US audience is about 49 percent; the tilt you return says how far THIS item's audience sits from that baseline.
demographics.income_band: Mirrors the US distribution with a higher median than women; men are the majority of six-figure earners and of investment-account and sports-betting-account holders.
demographics.education: Men now hold the minority of US bachelor's degrees among adults under 50; over-represented in trades and in engineering and computer science.
demographics.occupation_skew: Over-represented in construction, trades, transport, manufacturing, engineering, software, finance and sales; under-represented in healthcare, education and admin.
demographics.life_stage: Every stage. Fathers of young children under-index on parenting content relative to mothers; men 55 plus are the heaviest news, sports, history and western-film consumers.
geo_skew: Mirrors the US population. No DMA tilt for the lens as a whole.

values: This is a population, not a subculture. Half of every audience. Do not score men as a niche.

The signal that separates items is COMPOSITION. Fantasy football, sports betting, UFC, boxing, NFL RedZone, shooter and simulation games, crypto and day trading, cars and tools run 65 to 80 percent men. Sports leagues, sports-talk podcasts, action and sci-fi franchises, hip-hop streaming, rock and metal, war and spy thrillers, military history, tech and markets headlines run 55 to 65 percent men. News, drama, prestige TV, comedy, most streaming top-10s, most search terms sit near 50. Reality TV, daytime, home, cooking, wellness, parenting, beauty, true crime, romance, K-drama and Broadway run 20 to 40 percent men.

Men are the majority of the audience for live sports on every major league except the WNBA, for esports and Twitch, for YouTube long-form creators in gaming, science, cars, finance and comedy, and for podcasts in sports, politics, business, technology and long-form interview.
Men are the majority of buyers for games, consumer electronics, tools, auto parts, sports merchandise, spirits and craft beer; near parity on QSR, streaming subscriptions and Amazon.
Younger men are heavily on YouTube, Twitch, Kick, Discord and Reddit; older men on cable news, ESPN, History, Discovery, westerns and network sports.
aesthetics: Not applicable as a taste rule. Read the item for who its audience actually is.
psychographics.tone_they_respond_to: Not a scoring input. This lens measures audience composition, not tone.

themes_they_avoid: Nothing is avoided under this lens. Items simply carry a lower share where the audience is mostly women: romance and romantasy, Bravo and reality-dating, Hallmark and Lifetime, K-drama and K-pop, beauty and skincare, parenting and fertility, wedding and home-organizing content, Broadway, BookTok, celebrity and royal news, daytime TV, cozy and match-3 games.
filter_rules_for_agent: THIS LENS RANKS, IT DOES NOT FILTER. Score is secondary. The TILT is the deliverable: return, for each item, how the men share of ITS audience compares to the 49 percent baseline. tilt 1.0 means 49 percent men. tilt 1.5 means about 74 percent men (fantasy football, UFC, Call of Duty, Cleetus McFarland). tilt 0.7 means about 34 percent men (Bravo, Sabrina Carpenter, Emily Henry). tilt 0.3 means about 15 percent men (romance novels, Hallmark, Crumbl).

Anchor on published audience composition wherever it is known: Nielsen and network sales decks for TV, Edison and Spotify for podcasts and music, Circana and BookScan for books, ESA and Newzoo for games, Pew and Statista for platforms and search. When unknown, reason from the closest known comparable, not from a stereotype about the topic.

Streaming top-10 titles mostly sit between 0.8 and 1.2. Push above 1.25 only for live sports, sports docs, action and war franchises with a male lead and no romance line, hard sci-fi, most anime shonen, stand-up specials. Push below 0.75 only for romance, reality-dating, K-drama, Hallmark, Bridgerton-class and beauty or wedding formats.
